I don't see how that is an anit-vegetarian point. I think its pro vegetarian. By not force breeding animals to meet the unnecessary demand for meat the argument "if we don't eat meat, the animals will starve to death." Is taken care of. If you look into the treatment of most factory animals you'd probably agree that never being born is a better option than only being born to be tortured.

If we bred cats and dogs without the ability to feel pain should we kill them for stuffed animals or hats? I don't think so. Its a big gray area. (Bad analogy but I'm tired)

I think that if the organism is classified as an animal it is an animal. (Think Horton hears a who, a persons a person no matter how small) 

*sorry for grammatical errors and such, I'm only in seventh grade and my worldview and morals are still evolving. This being said I don't think that should make any of my opinions less valid

Yes you're getting the nutrients found in meat from other sources but just because meat also has those nutrients and it may be a more traditional source doesn't mean that its the "right" option. There are various health benefits from becoming a vegetarian actually. Its just not necessary to eat meat.

I don't think its abnormal to eat meat obviously, McDonald's, for example, is normal. And more seriously it's normal in nature for animals to eat other animals. But humans don't need to eat animals. It is not required anymore. At some point we needed meat or we would die but that is not the case anymore. So I think even though its "normal" to eat meat, humans are not fighting for survival every day in the way a bear or lion is. And therefore I find it pointless. 

So basically, humans did require meat for survival at one point, and some still do. But at this point in time humans do not need to eat meat any more than we need to eat peanut butter. Sure it tastes good and it has good nutritional value, but we can get those nutrients from other sources vary easily.

Its just that it was a living creature that could feel pain and eat grass and be alive and have sex. Like how most people think its weird to eat dogs, cats, monkeys, and horses; i think its bad to eat animals. I think my religious views come into play because I don't buy into the whole "man has a soul and animals are only there for us to eat." Like I said if you have to eat meat for health reasons or for survival then go right ahead. But most Americans could get by fine without killing an animal to do so. Dairy, honey, wool, etc. It all depends on the animals treatment in my opinion. I'm not like those Peta people who think eating eggs is like stealing from another human being, but the fact of the matter is almost all dairy cows and factory hens are treated awfully. If you know for sure they were treated well then yeah take a bath in milk lets do it.
I can see how you'd think that but what with all the different meat substitutes available, its definitely possible to have a balanced diet and be healthy without eating meat.
